mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: A small organizing cluster may impact the I-80 corridor of northeastern Ohio into northwestern Pennsylvania through 10 AM to noon EDT, accompanied by small to marginally severe hail and gusty winds. It is not clear that a severe weather watch is needed in the near term, but potential for stronger, more damaging gusts could increase later this morning, and trends are being monitored.

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A meso-beta scale cyclonic circulation has become better defined within a cluster of storms at least initially rooted above a shallow stable boundary layer. Strong convection has become focused in a short narrow corridor to the east/southeast of this circulation, which is approaching the Greater Cleveland vicinity. Based on recent acceleration in forward (eastward) propagation in excess of 30 kt, the convective system appears likely to track across the I-80 corridor into northwestern Pennsylvania between Franklin and Du Bois by 14-16Z. However, the boundary-layer across this region remains relatively stable, and this may only gradually begin to destabilize over the next few hours. Westerly ambient mean flow in the lower to mid-troposphere also remains relatively modest, on the order of 20-30 kt, so the extent to which potentially damaging wind gusts increases in the near term remains unclear.
